says: Today's lead tooling: the typecheck lock laws pass `FABRIKA_TYPECHECK_LOCK` to `typecheck.sh`, but no law shows that the script's Python opens the file at that path.
proof: Found by the review of pull request 1286 on 2026-11-14, by reading `scripts/caps.test.ts`: the laws set the variable to a lock file of their own and check only that two wrappers do not overlap. No assertion reads the lock file. A `typecheck.sh` that ignored the variable and locked its default path would still pass when no other typecheck runs on the machine.
cost: The laws can pass while they still share the machine's real lock, which is the flake pull request 1286 set out to remove. A fix: assert the test's own lock file exists after the first wrapper starts.
